messages:
Jordan Kim: FYI — customer 'Acme EU' reported intermittent slower tails today, looks like routing fell back to a smaller variant in eu-west unexpectedly. Anyone seen this in traces?
Priya Reddy: I saw a handful of requests where X-Redwood-Route matched 'eu-low-latency' but the model chosen was `gptx-4-quant` instead of `gptx-8`. Suspect capacity/burst policy triggered.
Miguel Santos: Can you paste a request trace id? want to confirm whether it was tier-based fallback vs region fallback.
Jordan Kim: trace 1958765432.ops. Attached below.
Jordan Kim: ```
route: eu-low-latency
customer_tier: enterprise
quota_remaining: 12000
selected_model: gptx-4-quant
fallback_reasons: ["capacity_pressure_region", "cost_policy"]
```
Alice Tran: Hmm 'capacity_pressure_region' + 'cost_policy' together suggests smart-routing tried preferred variant, failed, then applied fallback list for that route. But why cost_policy would kick for an enterprise tenant?
Priya Reddy: We recently changed fallback order for that route to prefer cheaper variants if queue_time > 150ms. Maybe the queuing metric was high in eu-west.
Elena Karpov: This is where the console UX is failing us — the request trace shows the selected model but not the decision chain. We should display the evaluation steps: policy match -> capacity check -> queue_time snapshot -> fallback applied and which rule fired.
Jordan Kim: +1. For debugging, we also need the routing headers in the raw request log. I want `X-Redwood-Routing-Policy`, `X-Redwood-Model-Choice`, and `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason` to be emitted to logging/observability.
Miguel Santos: Agree. Telemetry event names we could use: `routing.decision.start`, `routing.decision.evaluate`, `routing.decision.fallback`, `routing.decision.end`. Each should include fields: route, customer_id, customer_tier, region, selected_model, candidate_list, reason_codes, queue_time_ms, capacity_snapshot.
Priya Reddy: Example payload suggestion: ```json
{
  "event": "routing.decision.fallback",
  "route": "eu-low-latency",
  "customer_id": "acme-eu",
  "customer_tier": "enterprise",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "selected_model": "gptx-4-quant",
  "candidate_list": ["gptx-8","gptx-8-quant","gptx-4-quant"],
  "reason_codes": ["capacity_pressure_region","queue_time_threshold"],
  "queue_time_ms": 178
}
```
Alice Tran: Love that. Also add `rollout_version` and `policy_id` so we can tie to canary rules. We want to know if this happened because a new policy rollout was active.
Elena Karpov: UX idea: in traces, show a compact decision path UI with chips: [policy: eu-low-latency] -> [check: capacity ok? NO] -> [check: queue_time 178ms > 150ms] -> [fallback to gptx-4-quant reason=queue_time_threshold]. Clicking a chip expands the policy config and the telemetry events.
Jordan Kim: Can we store last 3 decisions for a trace so the console can replay the path? Like a lightweight playback of evaluate -> retry -> fallback.
Miguel Santos: Technically easy — we already emit events at each step. We need to persist them for X days (default 7) and surface in Console's trace view. Cost impact minimal if we sample at 10% and always store full traces for enterprise tenants.
Priya Reddy: Sampling rules: always keep full decision traces for enterprise and for any request that triggers fallback. Sample N% for others.
Alice Tran: SLA concern: should we change fallback trigger thresholds for enterprise to avoid cost-based fallbacks? Enterprise customers expect consistent perf; maybe prefer cross-region routing before cheaper variants.
Elena Karpov: UI for that: a toggle in the route config: 'prefer_performance_over_cost for tiers [list]'. The Console should display a small badge when that toggle differs from global default.
Jordan Kim: Action items: 1) Miguel + Priya add telemetry event schema and header names to the routing service. 2) Alice + Elena prototype decision path UI panel for traces. 3) Ops to enable always-store for enterprise and fallback events. 4) We'll add an alert if rate of `routing.decision.fallback` for enterprise > 1% in region for 5m.
Miguel Santos: I'll open a PR for telemetry and headers, will include the example JSON and the field list.
Priya Reddy: I'll update the policy engine to attach `policy_id` + `rollout_version` to every event. Also add a small backoff to queue_time threshold during canaries.
ops-bot: Created incident ticket INF-412: Investigate routing fallback frequency for eu-west (linked traces: 1958765432).
Jordan Kim: Thanks — once PRs land we can re-run the Acme trace and verify the new headers/events show up in Console.
Elena Karpov: One more UX ask: when a fallback happens, surface a one-click 'Why this?' modal that compiles the rule text + telemetry snapshot + link to candidate models and the decision timeline. Keeps CS folks from filing tickets.
Miguel Santos: Noted. I'll add a `why_url` field in the event that points to a pre-signed Console view for the trace.
Priya Reddy: That should help. ok moving to implement, will ping when draft PRs are up. :rocket:
